Digest PDF generation hit two environment issues this run: PIL's compiled _imaging extension was broken (same category as prior runs' documented issues) -- fixed with `pip install --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir pillow`, which was sufficient on its own this time (no PIL stubbing needed). The system `cryptography` package's rust bindings also panicked on import (via fpdf2's unused PKCS12/AES support) -- fixed the same way with `pip install --ignore-installed --no-cache-dir cryptography cffi` (the Debian-installed version couldn't be cleanly uninstalled, --ignore-installed shadowed it instead); no module stubbing was needed this run, unlike some prior runs. Separately, this fpdf2 version's `multi_cell` defaults to new_x=RIGHT rather than LMARGIN, which broke multi-item digest text (leftover cursor position triggered 'Not enough horizontal space') -- fixed by passing new_x="LMARGIN", new_y="NEXT" explicitly; also replaced the literal em dash in the title string with an ASCII-safe substitute, since core Helvetica can't encode U+2014.
